breaks.quote: If the honest answer is no, something good has to go.
breaks.why: The ask to prune rests almost wholly on the author's one story, so the reader is told to cut good things without a case built from their own life.

breaks.quote: 2 to 3 hours went to these small, everyday things, and to simply keeping all of them in my head.
breaks.why: The cost of the old way is named in one sentence inside the author's story and left, not argued or shown in the reader's own days.

breaks.quote: You may not have a rose garden or a dog to walk, but you probably have your own list.
breaks.why: The reader's own case is one short paragraph just before the ask, so why their way fails them and why the change is worth its cost is named, not built.
